sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitter Linda Jordan, SIL/ILN). 2018. Change Request Number 2018-085: create [pnd] Mpinda (adopted 2019-01-25). Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Identity/classification only: Bantu Zone H (Guthrie 1970), closest coded language Kimbundu [kmb]; lexical similarity 64% with Ndongo, 54% with Nsume, 47% with Kibala; ancestors include Sama, Waku Kungo and Kisolongo (Kikongo) settlers. Sources named: Jordan & Manuel 2016 (SIL ESR 2016-009); Jordan & Manuel 2017 'Kwanza Sul II: Hele, Mpinda e Ndongo' (ILN Luanda, 'Unpublished material'); Menezes 2011; Guthrie 1970.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2018. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: Mpinda [pnd] (companion form to CR 2018-085).
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Autonym Mpinda, no alternate names; ~18,000 speakers of ~30,000 Ampinda; coastal lowlands south of Porto Amboim town (-10.76, 13.72); Niger-Congo Bantu H.2; 'What written literature.. exist in this language?: None'; no dictionaries or grammars listed under sources.

sources.citation: Jordan, Linda & Isata Manuel. 2016. Sociolinguistic Survey of Kwanza Sul Province, Angola: With a Special Focus on the Kimbundu Variants. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2016-009. Dallas: SIL International. 37 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (dialect mapping, recorded-text tests, lexicostatistics). Mpinda appears only in identity/comprehension tables and origin history (Sect. 1.2, printed p. 4); conclusions (printed p. 20): 'The degree of intelligibility between Ndongo and Mpinda is still unknown' and recommends 'Documentation of the variants of Porto Amboim municipality (Mpinda, Ndongo)'. Appendix C wordlists cover Lubolo, Kibala, Ucela and Nsume only -- no Mpinda wordlist. The strings stress/accent/tone/pitch/prosod/suprasegmental/syllable do not occur anywhere in the text.

sources.note: The only document with first-hand Mpinda linguistic data (April 2017 Porto Amboim fieldwork: 600-item wordlist, RTT, dialect mapping) and the basis of ISO code pnd; a transcribed wordlist may carry tone/stress marks or a note on prosody. Ask SIL (Linda Jordan) or the ILN Luanda for a copy, or check whether it was later released as an SIL Electronic Survey Report.
